prTitle: fix: update the request method for the setAccountInfo API.

analysis.summary: Changing setAccountInfo from GET to POST introduces a data serialization bug where a JavaScript object is sent with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded without proper URL encoding, causing malformed request bodies.

bugs.title: Form-urlencoded Content-Type with unserialized object payload
bugs.description: The axios.post call sends a JavaScript object as the request body while setting Content-Type to application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Axios does not automatically convert objects to form-urlencoded format, resulting in the server receiving [object Object] or malformed data instead of properly encoded key-value pairs.
bugs.risk: HIGH: The API will receive malformed payload data, causing the setAccountInfo call to fail or corrupt customer data (UID, profile data, phones). This breaks the customer edit functionality entirely.

suggestions.suggestion: Use URLSearchParams or a library like 'qs' to serialize the request payload when using application/x-www-form-urlencoded Content-Type.
suggestions.rationale: Axios does not automatically convert JavaScript objects to form-urlencoded strings. Proper serialization ensures the API receives correctly formatted data.

suggestions.suggestion: Consider migrating to application/json Content-Type if the Gigya/setAccountInfo endpoint supports it.
suggestions.rationale: Using JSON would eliminate the need for manual JSON.stringify of nested objects (data, profile, phones) and simplify the code while reducing serialization errors.

suggestions.suggestion: Add integration tests that verify the actual HTTP request body format and Content-Type headers for setAccountInfo.
suggestions.rationale: This change affects the wire format of API calls. Tests should catch mismatches between declared Content-Type and actual payload serialization.

notBugs.reason: Gigya APIs expect complex objects (profile, data) as JSON strings within form-urlencoded fields. The explicit JSON.stringify calls are correct for this API contract.

notBugs.topic: Change from GET params to POST body
notBugs.reason: Intentional change per PR title. POST is appropriate for update operations and prevents sensitive data from appearing in URL query strings.
